title: Your profile, password and email signature
summary: Change your photo, name, job title, phone number, sign-in email and password, and find your email signature.

body.text: **Settings → My account → Profile & sign-in** is the one part of Settings everyone can open. It holds your own details and how you sign in. Nobody else can change these for you, except an owner resetting a forgotten password.
Your photo and personal details
Your details appear on records you're assigned to, on messages you send and in your email signature.

items: Open **Settings**, then **Profile & sign-in**.
To add or change your photo, choose a picture — JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 3 MB.
Under **Personal details**, fill in **Full name**, and optionally **Job title** and **Phone number** (for example +27 82 123 4567).
Save.

body.text: Changing the email you sign in with

items: Under **Sign-in email**, type the new **Email address**.
Enter your **Current password** to confirm it's you.
Save. From now on you sign in with the new address.

body.text: Changing your sign-in email signs you out on your other devices. Sign in again there with the new address.
Changing your password

items: Open **Password** and press **Change**.
Enter your current password, then a new one: at least 12 characters, with both letters and numbers.
Save.

body.text: Changing your password signs you out on every other device straight away. The device you're using stays signed in.
Your email signature

Open **Email signature** and press **View & edit**. If your workspace uses the Email signatures feature, the link takes you to the **Email signatures** page, where everyone's signature is managed in one place.
Also on this page

items: **Two-factor authentication** and **Passkeys** — see *Two-factor sign-in and passkeys*.
**Push notifications** — turn alerts on for this device. See *Notifications and alerts on your phone*.

body.text: If something goes wrong

rows: New password must be at least 12 characters and contain letters and numbers.
Make it longer, and include at least one letter and one number.
Check Caps Lock and try again. If you've forgotten it, sign out and use **Forgot password?** on the sign-in page, or ask an owner to reset it.
Choose a password different from your current password.
Pick a new password you haven't used here.

title: Two-factor sign-in and passkeys
summary: Add a second step to signing in with an authenticator app or email codes, or sign in with your fingerprint or face using a passkey.

body.text: Two-factor sign-in adds a second step after your password, so your account stays safe even if someone learns your password. A **passkey** goes further: you sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN instead of typing a password at all. Both are set up under **Settings → Profile & sign-in**.
Turning on two-factor with an authenticator app

items: Open **Two-factor authentication** (it shows **Off**) and press **Set up**.
Choose **Set up authenticator app**.
Scan the code on screen with an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator, Authy or 1Password.
Type the 6-digit code the app shows into **Enter the 6-digit code it shows** and press **Verify & enable**.
Save the **backup codes** that appear. Each one works once if you lose your phone.

body.text: The backup codes are shown only once. Keep them somewhere safe and away from your phone, such as a password manager. Without your phone or a backup code, an owner has to reset your two-factor before you can sign in.
Email codes as a backup

Tick **Also allow email sign-in codes as a backup** to be sent a code by email at sign-in. It's handy if you lose your phone, but it means anyone who can get into your email could also get into the CRM.
Turning two-factor off

items: Open **Two-factor authentication** and press **Manage**.
Under **Turn off — enter a current code**, type a code from your authenticator app.
Press **Disable 2FA**.

body.text: Passkeys: sign in with your fingerprint or face

items: Open **Passkeys** and press **Set up** (or **Manage** if you already have one).
Press **Add a passkey** and follow your device's prompt (fingerprint, face or PIN).
Give it a **Device name** you'll recognise later, such as "Work laptop" or "My iPhone".

body.text: Add a passkey on each device you use. The list shows when each was added and last used. Remove one you no longer use, such as an old phone, with **Remove passkey**.
If you see "This browser doesn't support passkeys", use Safari, Chrome or Edge on a device with a fingerprint reader, Face ID or a PIN.
Locked out?

Use one of your backup codes at the sign-in prompt. If you have none, ask a workspace owner: on **Settings → Team & roles** they can press **Reset 2FA** next to your name. You'll then sign in with your password only until you set two-factor up again.

title: Notifications and alerts on your phone
summary: Turn on alerts for each phone and computer, test them, and (owners) choose which events alert the team.

body.text: The CRM can alert you on your phone or computer when something needs you — a new lead, a customer message, a signed quote, a meeting about to start. Alerts are switched on **per device**, and owners decide which kinds of event send them at all.
Turning alerts on for this device

items: Open **Settings → Notifications** (or **Push notifications** on **Profile & sign-in**).
Under **Push on this device**, turn alerts on and allow them when your browser or phone asks.
Press **Send test notification** to check one arrives.

body.text: Every phone and computer is switched on separately. On a phone, install the CRM to your home screen first — that's what lets alerts appear on your lock screen. See *Install it on your phone & get notifications*.
To stop alerts on a device, press **Disable on this device** there.
What sends an alert (owners)
**What sends a notification** applies to the whole team. Untick a type to silence it on everyone's devices.

rows: A lead arrives from Facebook, Instagram, your website or WhatsApp
A new Messenger or Instagram message
The WhatsApp assistant hands a chat to a person
A chatbot flow's "Tell someone" step names you
An online booking lands in the workshop diary
Portal service requests, Support cases, Customer uploads, Warranty claims, Profile change requests
A customer does that from the customer portal
A customer opens their signing link
A customer asks a question or requests changes on the signing page
A customer replies to an email
A customer's mail server refused an email — only to whoever sent it
A customer clicks the banner under your email signature — only to whoever wrote the email
A customer downloads a file you sent as a secure link — only to whoever sent it
A referred deal is won and a fee is due
An important change on a competitor's page you watch
Something in the CRM failed (at most one alert every 30 minutes)
Monthly security check results and problems with the AI service
The nightly backup didn't run (at most one a day)
An hour before a timed meeting or test drive — tapping it opens Google Maps
Someone @mentions you in a note — only to you
A note, stage change, customer reply or job update on a record you watch — only to you
A question you scheduled with the assistant has been answered — only to you

body.text: Only owners can change the team-wide list. Everyone can switch alerts on or off on their own devices.
If alerts don't arrive

items: Press **Send test notification**. If nothing appears, check your phone or browser allows notifications for the CRM.
On an iPhone, alerts only work once the CRM is added to your home screen and opened from there.
Check the alert type is still ticked under **What sends a notification** (ask an owner).

title: Company profile: your business details
summary: Set your business name, contact details and logo, which appear on your documents, emails and sign-in screen.

body.text: **Settings → Company profile** holds your business's own details. They're printed on your quotes, invoices and other documents and used in your emails. Only owners can open it.
Your business details

rows: The name on your documents and emails
A short line under your name, for example "Family-owned since 1998"
Your social pages, where a document shows them

items: Open **Settings → Company profile**.
Fill in the details you want to show. Leave a box empty if it doesn't apply.
Save.

body.text: Names for records

Further down, **Names for records** lets you use your own word for a record — for example "Enquiry" instead of "Lead", or "Work order" instead of "Job card". Your words appear in the menu, page titles and buttons. Leave a box blank to keep the standard word.

title: Managing team members and their access
summary: Add a team member, reset a password or two-factor, sign someone out everywhere, and disable or reactivate an account.

body.text: Everyone who works in your workspace is managed on **Settings → Team & roles**, under **User security**. Only owners see these controls.
Adding a team member

items: Open **Settings → Team & roles**.
Press **Add a team member**.
Enter their **Full name**, **Email** and a starting **Password** (at least 12 characters, with letters and numbers).
Press **Add team member**, then give them their email and password.

body.text: New people start with the **Sales representative** role. Change their roles under **Role assignments** on the same page (see *Roles and permissions*). Each email address can only be used once.
What you can do for each person
The **User security** table shows each person's status, **Last login** and **Failed logins**. Next to everyone except yourself:

rows: Signs them out on every phone and computer straight away. They can sign in again with their password.
Sets a new password you choose (at least 12 characters, letters and numbers). They're signed out everywhere and can change it themselves afterwards.
Shown when they use two-factor sign-in. Turns it off so they can sign in with their password, for example after losing their phone. They should set it up again.
Stops them signing in at all, without deleting anything they did. Use it when someone leaves.
Lets a disabled person sign in again.

body.text: When someone leaves, press **Disable**. Their records, notes and history stay in the CRM; they just can't sign in. If they had the assistant linked to their WhatsApp, unlink it on **Settings → Sessions & devices** too.
Auto sign-out
How long someone can be idle before being signed out is set on **Settings → Sessions & devices**. See *Sessions and devices*.
If something goes wrong

rows: Name, email and a password of at least 12 characters containing letters and numbers are required.
Fill in all three; make the password longer and include letters and numbers.
A user with that email already exists.
That address already has an account. Check the table — they may already be here — or use a different address.

title: Roles and permissions
summary: Decide what each person can see and do by giving them roles — named sets of permissions.

body.text: What someone can see and do is decided by their **roles**. A role is a named set of permissions — for example "Sales representative" or "Workshop manager". Give a person one or more roles and they get every permission in them. Owners always have every permission.
Roles are on **Settings → Team & roles**, under **Roles & permissions**.
The built-in roles

Your workspace starts with ready-made roles such as **Sales representative**, **Sales manager**, **CRM administrator**, **Marketing user** and **Read-only auditor**, plus **Technician** and **Workshop manager** when the workshop is switched on. You can adjust their permissions, but they're meant as sensible starting points.
Creating your own role

items: Press **Create role**.
Give it a **Role name**, for example "Sales manager", and create it.
Open the role and tick the permissions it should have.
Press **Save permissions**.

body.text: Giving people roles

items: Scroll to **Role assignments**.
Tick the roles each person should have.
Press **Save** on their row.

body.text: Seeing everything versus seeing your own

Many areas come as a pair of permissions — for example **View all leads** and **View owned and team leads**. "Owned and team" means the records someone created, is assigned to, or that belong to a team they're in or manage.
A common set-up: sales reps get the "owned and team" permissions, and managers get the "all" ones.
A permission change applies on the person's next click — they don't need to sign out.

title: Teams and who sees which leads
summary: Group people into teams so team members and their manager can see each other's leads and customers.

body.text: Teams decide what people with "owned and team" access can see. Someone like that sees their own records, plus the records of every team they belong to or manage. Teams are on **Settings → Team & roles**.
Creating a team

items: Press **Create team**.
Enter a **Name**, for example "Sales floor", optionally choose a **Manager**, and add a **Description** if useful.
Create it.

body.text: Adding and removing members

items: Open the team.
Use **Add member…** to add someone. Remove someone with the control next to their name.
Change the manager, description or whether the team is active, then press **Save team**.

body.text: You need the **Create teams and manage membership** permission to change teams. With only **View teams**, you see them but can't edit.

title: Sales pipelines and stages
summary: Set up one or more sales processes, each with its own stages, win chances and closing results.

body.text: A pipeline is the series of stages a lead moves through, from first contact to won or lost. You can run several — for example one for walk-in retail customers and another for fleet sales — each with its own stages. Pipelines are on **Settings → Pipeline**.
You need the **Create and configure sales pipelines and stages** permission.
Creating a pipeline

items: Press **Create pipeline**.
Enter a **Name**, choose a **Type** (Retail, Fleet / B2B, Hospitality, Partner / Dealer, Service upsell or Other sales) and an optional **Description**.
Tick **Make this the default pipeline** if new leads should start here.
Create it, then add its stages.

body.text: Setting up stages
Open a pipeline and use **+ Add stage**. For each stage you can set:

rows: How the stage appears on the lead board
The usual chance of winning a lead at this stage — used by the sales forecast
A lead left here longer than this is flagged as going stale
Marks the stage as the end of the road, with a result of **Won** or **Lost**
Something staff must fill in before a lead can be moved into this stage

body.text: Use **Move up** and **Move down** to put stages in order, then **Save stage**.
Archiving a pipeline
A pipeline can only be archived when it has never held a lead, and the default pipeline can't be archived. Make another pipeline the default first.

title: Customer portal access
summary: Let a customer see another account's or a fleet's records in the portal, and approve changes customers ask to make to their details.

body.text: **Settings → Portal access** controls two things in the customer portal: who can see more than their own records, and changes customers ask to make to their contact details.
You need the **Manage delegated customer-portal access and profile approvals** permission, and the customer portal must be switched on for your workspace.
Approving changes customers ask for
When a customer asks to change their details in the portal, it waits under **Pending profile changes**. Check the new values, then either:

items: **Approve & apply** — updates their record (you can add an optional note), or
**Reject** — leaves their record as it is. A reason is required, so the customer knows why.

body.text: Letting a customer see more
Normally a portal user sees only their own records. You can let them see another account — for example a company administrator seeing the company's records — or a whole fleet.

items: Under **Grant contact/account access** (or **Grant fleet access**), choose the **Portal user**.
Choose the **Contact or account to expose** (or the **Fleet to expose**).
Pick a **Role** — Viewer, Manager or Owner — and press **Grant access**.

body.text: Current access is listed with its role and status. Press **Revoke** to take it away.
Related guides

items: Managing fleets

title: Security checks
summary: The platform's monthly security check: what it looks at, how to run it, and how to read the results.

body.text: **Settings → Security checks** runs a set of automatic checks on the system's security — keys, what's exposed to the internet, backups and accounts — and gives a score out of 100.
Only the platform owner sees this screen. It's about the whole system, not one workspace.
Running the checks

items: Open **Settings → Security checks**.
Run the checks. It can take up to a minute.
Read each result — **Pass**, **Warn** or **Fail** — and the suggested fix for anything that didn't pass.

body.text: The top of the page shows the score, the **Last run** date, **AI health** (whether the AI service is working) and **AI usage (month)**.
The checks also run by themselves on the 1st of every month, and the **History** list keeps every past score.

title: Backups
summary: How your data is backed up every night, how to check the backups are healthy, and what happens if data ever needs restoring.

body.text: Everything in the CRM is backed up automatically every night, encrypted, and checked after it's made. **Settings → Backup & recovery** shows that this is happening.
Only the platform owner sees this screen. Workspace owners don't need to do anything — backups cover every workspace.
What the screen shows

items: **Latest automated run** — when the last backup ran and whether it succeeded.
**Database copies** and **Asset snapshots** — how many restore points are kept. The newest 30 are kept.
**Last verification** — when a backup was last checked to be complete and readable.

body.text: Checking or making a backup now

items: **Run backup** makes a fresh restore point straight away.
**Verify** on any kept backup checks it's complete.
**Encrypted file** downloads a copy for safekeeping elsewhere.

body.text: A downloaded backup can only be opened with the system's encryption key. Keep that key stored safely, separately from the backups.
If data ever needs restoring

Restoring is done by the platform owner, carefully and step by step: the data is restored to a separate copy first, checked, and only then switched over. It's never a one-click button, so a mistake can't overwrite live data.
Deleted something by accident? Check **Trash** first — most deleted items can be restored there for 60 days, with no backup needed.

title: Sessions and devices
summary: See who is signed in on which devices, sign out a device or a person, and set how long before idle staff are signed out.

body.text: **Settings → Sessions & devices** lists every phone and computer your team is signed in on, so you can sign out a device or a person straight away. Only owners can open it.
Auto sign-out after inactivity
At the top, choose how long someone can be idle before they're signed out — from 15 minutes to 24 hours — and press **Save**.
Saving signs everyone else in your workspace out, so they sign in again under the new rule. Do it at a quiet time. Everyone also signs in again at least every 72 hours, whatever this is set to.
What's listed

Each person shows their signed-in devices: the browser and type of device, the internet address, when they signed in and when they were last active. Only sign-ins that can still be used are listed. Phone app sign-ins are marked **Mobile app · 7-day session** — they last a week.
A device tagged **May already be signed out** signed in before this list could tell for sure. It isn't counted as active, but you can still revoke it to be certain.
Signing someone out

items: **Revoke** next to a device signs out just that device.
**Sign out all** on a person's card signs them out everywhere.

body.text: Use **Sign out all** when a phone or laptop is lost, or when someone leaves. Then press **Disable** on **Team & roles** so they can't sign back in.
The assistant on WhatsApp
If someone linked their WhatsApp number to the assistant, it shows on their card with **Unlink**. **Sign out all** also ends it.

title: Integrations: connecting your other services
summary: Connect WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, X, Threads, email, Xero and Google reviews, and see which connections need attention.

body.text: **Settings → Integrations** is where the CRM connects to the other services your business uses. Each connection shows whether it's **Connected** or **Not set up**, and anything that has stopped working is listed first under **Needs attention**.
What you can connect

rows: WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and Instagram (with Facebook and Instagram lead ads), X, Threads, and SMS for one-time codes
Outgoing email from your own mail server, and incoming replies brought into the Inbox
Xero — send invoices and bring payments back

body.text: Some services are set up once for the whole CRM by your CRM provider rather than by each business — the AI the CRM uses, voice, Telegram, Google Maps address suggestions and taking leads from a website. If you need one of these changed, ask your CRM provider.
Connecting a service

items: Find the service and open its card.
Use its connect button where it has one (for example **Connect WhatsApp**), or fill in the details from the other service and press **Save**.
The card changes to **Connected** once it works.

body.text: Passwords and keys you enter are stored encrypted and never shown again. To change one, type the new value and save.
Step-by-step guides

Most services need a few steps on their side too. Follow the guide for the one you're connecting: **Connect WhatsApp with one button**, **Connecting WhatsApp Business (Cloud API)**, **Connecting Facebook Messenger**, **Connecting Instagram DMs**, **Connecting Facebook & Instagram Lead Ads**, **Connecting Google reviews**, **Connect X to the Social inbox** and **Xero: sending invoices to your books**.

title: Products and stock labels
summary: Where to manage your product catalogue, and how to set up labels for organising stock.

body.text: Under **Settings → Workshop & stock** you'll find **Products** (your catalogue) and **Stock labels**. Both appear when stock is switched on for your workspace.
Products
**Products** opens your product catalogue — the models, colours, codes and prices used by stock, leads, quotes and vehicles. See *Managing the product catalogue*.
Stock labels

Labels let you tag stock for your own organising — for example "Demo unit", "Consignment" or "Management hold". A label never changes where a unit is in its life (on order, available, sold and so on); it's just a tag.

items: Open **Settings → Stock labels**.
Under **Add a label**, enter a **Name** and pick a **Colour**.
Press **Add label**.

body.text: Removing a label also removes it from every unit that carried it.
